mstts:express-as.prosody: Have you ever felt that deep longing for real joy and fulfillment—something that goes beyond the ordinary, something that makes you stop and ask, "What’s my true purpose? What does happiness really mean?" Together, we’re about to explore a perspective that turns the search for pleasure and meaning on its head. In John Piper’s Desiring God: Meditations of a Christian Hedonist, we discover that the pursuit of joy isn’t just allowed in faith—it’s at the very heart of it. Imagine that: delighting in God isn’t just a side note, it’s the main event. Piper invites us to rethink everything we thought we knew about desire and devotion. Instead of seeing duty and self-denial as the core of spirituality, he suggests that the deepest satisfaction is found when God is treasured above everything else. As we walk through these meditations together, we’ll explore themes like worship, love, and how delight actually changes us from the inside out. This journey isn’t about adding another burden to your life—it’s about discovering how Christian hedonism calls us to embrace joy as a spiritual practice. Imagine prayer, worship, service, even life’s hardships—not as chores, but as moments to taste and see the goodness of God. So, if you’re ready to see faith not as a heavy obligation but as a passionate, joyful pursuit, you’re in the right place. Let’s set out on this path, where seeking God’s glory just might be the secret to the lasting happiness you’ve been searching for.
